raw_response: {"diagnosis": "The 27 extra raw rows are exactly the record_version=2 rows, so each duplicated txn_id has one version-1 row and one version-2 row. The silver step keeps both versions, and dedup-after-status-filter would keep a stale version-1 POSTED row if version 2 is a REVERSED correction. Keeping the highest record_version per txn_id before filtering POSTED gives one deterministic row per txn_id.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.6, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM (SELECT * FROM raw_transactions QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY record_version DESC, ingest_ts DESC) = 1) latest WHERE latest.status = 'POSTED';"}}
